title: Listing readiness scorecard and creative prototypes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, pragmatic readiness scorecard + first-pass creative prototypes intended to accelerate partner listings into cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). Use as a preflight for publishing, handoff to engineering/legal, and to generate marketing collateral for the listing page.

Context and constraints (quick):
- Target audience: Platform/product engineering teams evaluating Redwood Dedicated/Private for customers and partners.
- Primary goals: reduce friction for listing approvals, ensure minimum technical and legal gates met, and provide several marketing copy variants for quick A/B experiments on listing pages.
- This is an early draft: score thresholds are opinionated and should be adjusted after 2 marketplace launches.

1) Readiness scorecard (single-page scoring rubric)
- How to use: score each criterion 0 (missing) / 1 (partial) / 2 (complete). Multiply by weight. Sum and compare against target pass threshold (>= 80).

Criteria (weight in parentheses):
- Product description clarity (15): concise problem statement, 1–2 sentence "what" and 1 sentence "who".
- Value props and metrics (15): 3 prioritized bullets with measurable outcomes (latency, cost, reliability).
- Hero asset (10): screenshot or animated GIF that clearly shows the UI/console route or API call + important metric annotations.
- Tech integration checklist (15): deployment modes documented (hosted, dedicated, private), sample API call, auth flow, and sample terraform/ARM/Deployment Manager snippet.
- Compliance & security notes (10): mention KMS/HSM options, SOC2/HIPAA/ISO statuses or plan, data residency limitations.
- Billing and SKU mapping (10): defined SKU names, unit pricing, and trial/credit behavior.
- Support & SLA (8): support channels, escalation path, and SLA tiers listed.
- Legal & IP sign-offs (7): export control, model license summary, and partner MSA stub or checklist link.
- Localization and accessibility (5): primary locale included, alt text for assets, basic a11y checks.
- Page copy readiness (5): at least 2 headline options + 2 subheads and 3 CTAs.

Scoring example (mock):
- Product description clarity: 2 * 15 = 30
- Value props: 1 * 15 = 15
- Hero asset: 2 * 10 = 20
- Tech integration: 1 * 15 = 15
- Compliance: 1 * 10 = 10
- Billing: 2 * 10 = 20
- Support: 1 * 8 = 8
- Legal: 0 * 7 = 0
- Localization: 1 * 5 = 5
- Page copy: 2 * 5 = 10
Total = 133 (out of max 200). Normalize to percent = 66.5% -> needs work on legal/compliance to hit 80%.

Pass threshold guidance: target >= 80 (i.e., ~160/200). If between 65–80, allowed only with cross-functional signoff (legal + infra + GTM). Below 65, return to product/engineering for pre-listing work.

2) Quick tech/integration checklist (practical items with owners)
- Auth: OAuth2 + token exchange sample (owner: eng-integrations). Jira: GMKT-INT-21
- API sample: minimal POST/text generation request + example response (owner: eng-api).
- Deployment manifest: example helm + terraform snippet for Dedicated and Private (owner: eng-release).
- Monitoring: provide one CloudWatch/GCP Stackdriver/Azure Monitor dashboard sample and logging S3/GCS/Azure Blob retention guidance (owner: observability).
- Fallback policy: describe model variant fallback and rate limit behavior under capacity constraints (owner: serving-runtime).
- Cost guidance: per-token cost estimate and suggested quotas for trials (owner: product-pricing).

3) Creative prototypes: hero headlines, subheads, bullets, CTAs (short variants for quick experiments)
- Objective: produce short, testable copy variations that can be dropped into marketplace listing templates. Keep technical accuracy and avoid speculative claims (no promise of exact token costs).

Hero headline – technical focus (H1)
A: Enterprise LLM inference at predictable latency and cost
B: Ship LLM features without building inference stacks
C: Run models privately or in our hosted runtime—same API, predictable ops

Hero subhead (H2)
A: Dedicated GPU pools, automatic batching, and model rollouts with SLA-backed uptime
B: Same API for hosted, reserved, and VPC deployments—integrate in hours, scale with confidence
C: Reduce per-token spend with intelligent caching and runtime optimizations

3 Supporting bullets (one-liners for listing feature bullets)
- High-throughput serving runtime optimized for modern LLMs (quantization-friendly).
- Smart routing and automated fallbacks across regions and capacity tiers.
- Built-in observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns and rollout controls.

CTA variants (choose 1 for page)
- Get started with a free credit
- Request a dedicated capacity trial
- Contact sales for private deployment pricing

Short 100–120 char description for marketplace summary (two variants)
1) Redwood Inference: production-grade LLM serving with unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
2) Predictable LLM inference—low latency, cost controls, and enterprise-grade observability for product teams.

4) Asset list and minimal specs (what to attach to listing submission)
- Hero image (1920x1080) with overlay metrics (latency and throughput highlight). Provide PNG + optimized JPG.
- 3-step console screenshots (1280x720) showing model selection, routing policy, and rollout page. Annotate with captions.
- Short demo GIF (800x400) of streaming response from API to UI. Keep under 5s and 3 MB.
- One-pager PDF with product bulleted features and contact/SKU table (A4).

5) Marketplace-specific notes (quick callouts)
- AWS: include AMI/marketplace-product manifest if offering a private AMI or software subscription SKU. Confirm AWS Marketplace SKU mapping with finance.
- Azure: include offer ID and transactable plan metadata; check AppSource content restrictions for AI claims.
- GCP: provide images and machine type guidance for private listings. Validate GCP pricing template fields early.
- All: ensure trial behavior is documented (duration, token limits, cost center).

6) Acceptance gates (who signs off)
- Legal: confirm model licensing summary + MSA clauses (owner: legal).
- Security/Compliance: SOC2/HIPAA mapping or mitigation plan (owner: security).
- Finance/Billing: SKU mapping and revenue recognition note (owner: finance).
- Eng: tech manifest + sample deploy tested in target region (owner: eng-release).
- GTM: creative assets, two headline variants, and tracking parameters for listing analytics (owner: go-to-market).

7) Example Jira checklist to create (copy into a ticket template)
- [ ] Populate product description and three value bullets (GMKT-)
- [ ] Attach hero asset + 3 console screenshots
- [ ] Add sample API call and auth flow doc
- [ ] Confirm SKU mapping and trial terms with finance
- [ ] Security compliance summary attached
- [ ] Legal sign-off on claims + MSA stub

8) Open questions and risks (need answers before submit)
- Do we want to include model names on listing pages or keep generic "open models" language? (legal + product tradeoff on support surface)
- Which regions do we pre-populate for Private deployment images (US-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1)?
- Trial limits: token cap vs time window—what minimizes abuse while letting developers evaluate?
- Pricing framing: per-token vs per-request—what's compatible with each marketplace's pricing primitive?

9) Next steps and immediate owners
- GTM to canonicalize hero copy and pick primary CTA (owner: Aisha Patel) — due 2026-03-05
- Eng to produce one validated deployment manifest for AWS/eu-west-1 and attach logs dashboard (owner: Marco Ruiz) — due 2026-03-19
- Legal to draft model licensing summary for listing and add to Confluence (owner: Priya Singh) — due 2026-03-12

Notes / scratchpad (raw ideas):
- Consider a tiny interactive snippet on listing page that shows sample latency for a 512-token request vs a 2048-token request. Might be blocked by marketplace UI constraints but useful for sales collateral.
- Keep claims conservative: "optimized for" vs "cuts costs by".
- For screenshots, annotate with token count and latency to make performance tangible without promising SLAs.

Appendix: quick copy library (two short marketing blurbs we can reuse)
A: "Redwood Inference provides a consistent API for running LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private environments. Ship features faster with predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise observability."
B: "From prototypes to high-scale production, Redwood's serving runtime and rollout tooling reduce operational overhead so teams focus on product, not infra."

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12 A. Patel initial draft (scorecard + copy prototypes)
